record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: For N = 2 supersymmetric extensions of the Korteweg-de Vries equation with an odd Poisson structure, can one construct integrable extensions in which the bosonic fields do not evolve independently of the fermionic fields, but instead the bosonic evolution equations contain genuine fermionic interaction terms?

evidence.quote: A new N = 2 super KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure has been found recently in [7] but the resulting equations are somewhat less interesting in that the bosonic fields do not couple to the fermions in their time evolution. It would be of interest to see whether there are other 'odd' integrable extensions displaying fermionic interactions in the bosonic evolution equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider supersymmetric extensions of the Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation with N=2 supersymmetry, formulated in N=2 superspace with two bosonic fields and two fermionic (Grassmann-odd) fields. Equip the phase space with an odd (Grassmann-odd) Poisson bracket, i.e., a graded antisymmetric bracket of odd parity satisfying the graded Jacobi identity, and consider Hamiltonian evolution equations generated by such an odd Poisson structure together with a suitable Hamiltonian.

In the previously known construction of an N=2 super KdV equation built from an odd Poisson structure, the resulting time-evolution equations have the feature that the bosonic fields evolve autonomously, with no fermionic source terms appearing in the right-hand sides of their evolution equations (the fermionic fields enter only the fermionic evolution equations).

Question: Does there exist an integrable N=2 supersymmetric extension of the KdV equation, governed by an odd Poisson (Hamiltonian) structure, whose bosonic evolution equations contain genuine fermionic interaction terms — i.e., terms quadratic (or higher) in the fermionic fields that make the bosonic fields couple nontrivially to the fermions in their time evolution? If so, construct such an integrable system; if not, prove its nonexistence.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal continued activity on N=2 super KdV equations and odd/Grassmann-odd Hamiltonian structures (including supercomplexification methods producing odd Hamiltonian structures, and integrable super extensions related to K(-2,-2) and modified KdV equations). However, none of the readily available sources explicitly settle whether an integrable odd-Poisson N=2 super KdV extension exists in which the bosonic evolution is genuinely sourced by fermionic bilinears. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Integrable super extensions of K(-2,-2) equation
status_evidence.snippet: Supercomplexification is a special method of N=2 supersymmetrization in which the bosonic sector reduces to a complex version, with odd Hamiltonian structures appearing.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study odd Hamiltonian structures in N=2 supersymmetric integrable systems, but does not directly resolve the coupling question.

status_evidence.title: The Painlevé analysis for N=2 super KdV equations
status_evidence.snippet: Analysis of N=2 super KdV equations and their integrability properties.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature addresses N=2 super KdV integrability but does not definitively answer the odd-Poisson fermion-bosonic coupling question.

status_evidence.title: New integrable extensions of N=2 KdV and Boussinesq hierarchies
status_evidence.snippet: New integrable extensions of N=2 KdV hierarchies are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Several N=2 extensions are known, but the specific question on odd Poisson with bosonic-fermionic coupling is not clearly settled in the available sources.
